We are excited to announce that Phil has agreed to lead our rugby programmes in 2025 and beyond. 

As a former professional rugby coach, Phil’s background has seen him work from grass roots through to international professional players and clubs, domestically and abroad. facebook:1643647319253798_12299378124028.caption:
All of us who form Leamington RFC are  devastated to learn of the passing of Peter “Ladder” Gray following a courageous, long and brave battle with cancer.

The term legend can be overused but Pete really fulfilled and exceeded that moniker. 

Pete was a ferocious competitor on the pitch throughout his playing career with Leamington and a fantastic advocate and ambassador for the club and its people, even after he hung up his boots.

From a cup winning Colts side in 1981/82 which took him to Warwickshire and Midlands Colts selection he narrowly missed out on England Colts with Nigel Redman being selected ahead of him. He played at Rugby Lions and Leicester Tigers before joining Leamington first team in 1982/83  and stayed there for 10 plus years before sharing his wisdom  and competitive spirit with the sides down the club.

Pete progressed and served his time amongst the blazers and was President between 2014 and 2017.

Pete’s legacy at the club is further enhanced by his two sons Charlie and Edward who have both represented the club at first XV level with distinction.

Our thoughts prayers and love are extended to Pete’s family, at this difficult time.

facebook:1643647319253798_12350584485574.caption:

“There are some huge positives to take from last season, not least the culture and ambition that we’re building at the club. I can’t wait to bolster and build on this with a big wave of young talent joining us in the seniors.”

Louis Dunbavin’s performance in the cup final epitomised his season. Strong in the scrum and even more dominating in the loose, we are very excited to see where this ‘young’ prop goes as there is still plenty more to come.

On Sunday 15th June, Leamington Rugby Club Walking Rugby Team entered the inaugural Northampton Saints Walking Rugby Tournament at the Cinch Stadium Franklin’s Gardens home of Northampton Saints RFC. 

12 teams from around Warwickshire and Northamptonshire entered the competition.

Leamington started strong against Northampton Saints winning 8-2! As the competition continued the team went from strength to strength, and headed into the semi-final against Silhillians. The tense game saw Leamington go into the final with a 1-0 win.

The final game was against Bugbrooke, where Leamington won comfortably 4-2, taking home the competition trophy! 🏆🎉

💚 Keeping Your Child Safe in Sport Week 2025 💚

This week we’re proud to join clubs across the country in supporting NSPCC’s Keeping Your Child Safe in Sport Week - this year focusing on the vital role that parents and carers play in creating a positive sporting environment.

Meet our Safeguarding Lead, Hayley White 

“I am really looking forward to the season ahead and to building on the great work already taking place at the club. Safeguarding is at the heart of what we do, and we’re fully committed to ensuring every child enjoys rugby in a safe and supportive environment.

Positive parental behaviour plays a vital role in our safeguarding strategy, and we welcome the focus on responsible parenting as part of this year’s Keeping Your Child Safe in Sport Week.”

Thank you, Hayley, for all that you do to make Leam RFC a safe and welcoming place for our young players 💙💛❤️

#SafeInSport #OneClubOneLeam #NSPCC #KYCSIS25 #PlayYourPart

facebook:1643647319253798_13348436385789.caption:
At Leamington RFC, we’re proud of the positive culture built by our parents, coaches and volunteers.
Every weekend, that support helps our young players enjoy rugby in a safe, encouraging environment.

This week, as part of NSPCC Keeping Your Child Safe in Sport Week 2025, we’re highlighting how every parent and carer can make a difference - on and off the pitch.

A few simple reminders that go a long way:
💙 Cheer effort, not just results
💙 Respect referees, coaches and volunteers
💙 Be a role model for positive behaviour on the sidelines
💙 Talk to your child about what they enjoy most in rugby

Thank you to everyone who continues to play your part in making rugby a safe, supportive and enjoyable space for every child.

Before Leamington RFC, there was Leamington Rovers.

Founded in 1876, 50 years before today's club, they wore black shirts with a skull and crossbones on the front, played on Leam Terrace East, and had 100 members by 1879.

They reached the final of the inaugural Midland Counties Cup in 1882, losing to Moseley. They folded in 1886 when members stopped paying their subscriptions.

A century and a half on, the skull and crossbones returns. The Vets and the Lions have been wearing it on our centenary away strip, in tribute to the Rovers. 
💙❤️💛

#LeamingtonRFC #OneClubOneLeam  #LRFC100

facebook:1643647319253798_15208426699790.caption:
It started with a meeting.

14 April 1926. Leamington Town Hall. Around 70 people attended, chaired by the Deputy Mayor, G.W. Hawkins.

The reason they were there: 15 to 20 Leamington men were travelling to Kenilworth to play rugby every week. Why not form their own club?

Fred Barr took the chair of the new committee. The history describes him as the father of the club.

The rest is 100 years of history. 💙❤️💛

#LeamingtonRFC #OneClubOneLeam #LRFC100

We’re incredibly proud that nine members of Leamington RFC have been nominated for the England Rugby Volunteer of the Year Awards 25/26. Lucy Ramsbottom and Leanne Butters were at the Warwickshire RFU ceremony at Coventry RFC’s Nick Newbold Stadium yesterday representing the group.

Bill Dalton, Nora Mixova, Mark Pascoe, Harry Gooch, Julie Blackmore, Leanne Butters, Lucy Ramsbottom, Phil Evans, Hayley White, and John Raby - thank you.

Volunteers have kept this club alive and thriving for 100 years. None of what we do happens without people giving their time freely, week after week, because they love this club. It’s as true now as it was in 1926.

Congratulations to all nine. Well deserved, every one of you.

facebook:1643647319253798_15625416558091.caption:
Leamington station, 1935.

The New Zealand All Blacks stepped off the train and into town. The club put them up at the Regent Hotel and threw them a dance at the Palais de Danse. Some evening that must have been.

Sixteen years later, the Springboks came through. 630 people packed into Chesford Grange for the dance in their honour. When they left, they gave us two carved Springboks as a thank you. They have been leaping across our clubhouse wall ever since.

Two years after that, the All Blacks were back. They trained at our ground before playing the Midland Counties at Welford Road.

And in 1957, the Wallabies followed.

Four of the most famous touring sides in world rugby, all of them here, in Leamington. And two of them still with us on the clubhouse wall. 💙❤️💛

facebook:1643647319253798_15984050655561.caption:
In 1981, social secretary Trevor Roberts had an idea. Why not run the ball to Twickenham, like the Olympic torch relay, and raise some money on the way?

On 15 May 1982, a team of around 15 runners set off from Moorefields at 5am. Over twelve hours later, they ran onto the pitch at Twickenham. Robin Andrews had the honour of touching down.

They called it Running the Ball. It raised around £400, somewhere north of £1,500 in today’s money, with £225 going to Helen Ley House.

People enjoyed it so much they did it again. To Cardiff Arms Park in 1984. Across the sea to Lansdowne Road in 1985. Up to Edinburgh in 1986. Over the channel to Parc des Princes in 1987.

Every home union opened their stadium to a bunch of amateur runners. Every one except Scotland. Edinburgh Academicals stepped in and hosted them instead.

Over five years and five runs, several thousand pounds were raised for six different charities, including Helen Ley House, Leukaemia Research and Save the Children.

Italy hadn’t joined the championship yet. Maybe there’s some unfinished business.

Were you there? We’ve only got photos from the Cardiff leg. If you’ve got shots from Twickenham, Dublin, Edinburgh or Paris, we’d love to see them. 💙❤️💛

Today marks 56 years since Leamington RFC opened Moorefields.

The formal opening took place on 8th September 1970, conducted by Bill Ramsay, President of the RFU. The ground was named in honour of President Pip Moore, who had done so much to make the move possible. His term of office was extended to a third season so that he could preside over the opening of the ground that now bears his name.

Two representative sides played that day: a Leamington Invitation XV and a Warwickshire XV. Warwickshire won 22-6.

Who can spot an England international in a Leamington shirt? 👀

56 years later, it’s still home.

facebook:1643647319253798_16314618655837.caption:
🧠🏉 CONCUSSION AWARENESS DAY | 18 SEPTEMBER

Rugby is a physical game. We love the competition, the tackles, the teamwork and everything that comes with being part of a rugby club.

But there is one thing that will always come before the game: our players' health.

WHAT IS CONCUSSION?
Concussion is a brain injury. It can happen after a direct blow to the head, but it can also happen following a hit to the body that causes the head and brain to move rapidly.

And importantly, you don't have to lose consciousness to have a concussion.

Headache, dizziness, confusion, memory problems, poor balance, nausea, feeling foggy or simply not seeming like themselves can all be signs that something isn't right.

That's why everyone at Leamington RFC needs to know the 4 Rs: players, parents, coaches, first aiders, therapists and supporters.

🧠 1. RECOGNISE
Know the signs and symptoms. If something doesn't look right, take it seriously.

🛑 2. REMOVE
If concussion is suspected, remove the player from play immediately. There is no "playing on" and no same-day return to rugby in community rugby.

❤️ 3. RECOVER
Concussion needs time and appropriate management. Recovery should never be rushed, and players should follow the appropriate graduated return-to-play process.

🏉 4. RETURN
Returning to rugby is the final step, when the player is ready and has completed the appropriate return-to-play process safely.

OUR COMMITMENT TO PLAYER WELFARE
At our club, concussion awareness isn't just something we talk about on one day of the year.

We are proud to have:
✔️ 4 qualified physios and sports therapists for senior and colts rugby
✔️ A qualified first aider for every age group
✔️ Coaches, first aiders and therapists completing RFU HEADCASE training every year
✔️ A commitment to following RFU and World Rugby guidance

Because concussion can affect players of every age, from our youngest age groups through to senior rugby, everyone has a part to play in recognising when something isn't right.

If in doubt, sit them out.

The match, the training session and the result can wait. The player's brain can't. 💙❤️💛

#OneClubOneLeam #ConcussionAwareness #Headcase #GrassrootsRugby

facebook:1643647319253798_16384124015553.caption:
100 years ago today, Leamington RFC played its first game.

Saturday 25 September 1926. Coventry St Mark's were the visitors, and a good crowd turned out to watch.

It wasn't pretty. The local paper described a tight, scrappy contest fought out between the forwards, and St Mark's went in at half-time three points up.

After the break it was all Leamington. The pressure told on the right, and Russell went over almost exactly where the St Mark's try had come from. The conversion drifted just wide.

3-3. In the paper's words, "a well-fought game ended with honours even."

The first Leamington XV: Kench; Peers, Foss, Hughes, Price; Clow, Chapman; Lewis, Russell, Millen, Smith, Jacox, Walkley, Scovell, Barr.

Here's to the next 100. 💙❤️💛

instagram:17865935820642090.caption:
In 1981, social secretary Trevor Roberts had an idea. Why not run the ball to Twickenham, like the Olympic torch relay, and raise some money on the way?

On 15 May 1982, a team of around 15 runners set off from Moorefields at 5am. Over twelve hours later, they ran onto the pitch at Twickenham. Robin Andrews had the honour of touching down.

They called it Running the Ball. It raised around £400, somewhere north of £1,500 in today’s money, with £225 going to Helen Ley House.

People enjoyed it so much they did it again. To Cardiff Arms Park in 1984. Across the sea to Lansdowne Road in 1985. Up to Edinburgh in 1986. Over the channel to Parc des Princes in 1987.

Every home union opened their stadium to a bunch of amateur runners. Every one except Scotland. Edinburgh Academicals stepped in and hosted them instead.

Over five years and five runs, several thousand pounds were raised for six different charities, including Helen Ley House, Leukaemia Research and Save the Children.

Italy hadn’t joined the championship yet. Maybe there’s some unfinished business.

Were you there? We’ve only got photos from the Cardiff leg. If you’ve got shots from Twickenham, Dublin, Edinburgh or Paris, we’d love to see them. 💙❤️💛

instagram:17887174188289731.caption:
Backs & Forwards Coaches - Jake Andrews & Tom Lane

Jake ‘Glass Cheeks’ Andrews moved into the coaching team after retiring early as a player through injury. He has taken to coaching like a duck to water, navigating the unique challenges of leading the second team. This season sees Jake take the reins of the first team backline, and with the pace and power at his disposal we are all excited to see what he can unlock. 

We are also very pleased that Tom Lane has agreed to bring another season of teaching the next generation, of the ‘dark arts’ of the game. His insight around set piece was instrumental, particularly in our mauling game, a non traditional characteristic of previous Leamington sides but now a primed weapon. Looking at the fixture list year we're sure we will see Tom’s magic tricks against some big packs.

instagram:17922816069143581.caption:
One of our founder members played in the very first season of Leamington RFC.
His name was Bill Heynes. He's front row, second from left.

After hanging up his boots, he went on to lead the team that designed the Jaguar XK engine, one of the most celebrated engines in British automotive history.

In the 1920s, he had submitted a twin overhead camshaft design to the Institute of Mechanical Engineers. He was told he was too far ahead of his time. The Japanese adopted the same layout in the 1970s. 💙❤️💛

103-0.

The biggest win in 1st XV history. Against new opponents Bletchley, 1993/94.

17 tries. It was Kenny Johnson's first game as permanent scrum-half. A Leamington junior himself, Kenny had already played for the Midlands and represented a combined Midlands & North side against England in the international trials. The following season he was capped by Warwickshire.

But the highlight belonged to a forward. Second row Carl Fripp picked up deep in his own half, burst through a string of tackles, and ran the length of the pitch to score.

Six foot nine. Barely into his second season of rugby. In the team photo he's stood next to the late Peter Gray, and somehow makes even him look small.

Still the 1st XV record, more than 30 years on.

instagram:17976512595102802.caption:
Leamington station, 1935.

The New Zealand All Blacks stepped off the train and into town. The club put them up at the Regent Hotel and threw them a dance at the Palais de Danse. Some evening that must have been.

Sixteen years later, the Springboks came through. 630 people packed into Chesford Grange for the dance in their honour. When they left, they gave us two carved Springboks as a thank you. They have been leaping across our clubhouse wall ever since.

Two years after that, the All Blacks were back. They trained at our ground before playing the Midland Counties at Welford Road.

And in 1957, the Wallabies followed.

Four of the most famous touring sides in world rugby, all of them here, in Leamington. And two of them still with us on the clubhouse wall. 💙❤️💛

#LeamingtonRFC #OneClubOneLeam #LRFC100

He started on a field in Leamington. 💙❤️💛

instagram:18013404497757764.caption:
All of us who form Leamington RFC are  devastated to learn of the passing of Peter “Ladder” Gray following a courageous, long and brave battle with cancer.

The term legend can be overused but Pete really fulfilled and exceeded that moniker. 

Pete was a ferocious competitor on the pitch throughout his playing career with Leamington and a fantastic advocate and ambassador for the club and its people, even after he hung up his boots.

From a cup winning Colts side in 1981/82 which took him to Warwickshire and Midlands Colts selection he narrowly missed out on England Colts with Nigel Redman being selected ahead of him. He played at Rugby Lions and Leicester Tigers before joining Leamington first team in 1982/83  and stayed there for 10 plus years before sharing his wisdom  and competitive spirit with the sides down the club.

Pete progressed and served his time amongst the blazers and was President between 2014 and 2017.

Pete’s legacy at the club is further enhanced by his two sons Charlie and Edward who have both represented the club at first XV level with distinction.

Our thoughts prayers and love are extended to Pete’s family, at this difficult time.

instagram:18050580302754556.caption:
It started with a meeting.

14 April 1926. Leamington Town Hall. Around 70 people attended, chaired by the Deputy Mayor, G.W. Hawkins.

The reason they were there: 15 to 20 Leamington men were travelling to Kenilworth to play rugby every week. Why not form their own club?

Fred Barr took the chair of the new committee. The history describes him as the father of the club.

The rest is 100 years of history. 💙❤️💛

We are excited to announce that Phil has agreed to lead our rugby programmes in 2025 and beyond. 

As a former professional rugby coach, Phil’s background has seen him work from grass roots through to international professional players and clubs, domestically and abroad. His local success saw him win National 3 on two occasions with Broadstreet RFC whilst also working at RGS Worcester as Head of Coaching and latterly Head of Performance as a Level 3 RFU coach.

“I’ve been fortunate to work within many clubs over the years but there is something special here at Leamington that keeps drawing me back. I’ve never known a club so focussed on the wellbeing and welfare of its players and coaches so keen to develop talent. This translates into a freedom on the field that sees us play one of the exciting flowing styles of rugby going. Long may that continue”

"Already we have key players committing to the new season we will be announcing a number of new signings over the coming weeks. I've never been more excited about the start of a new season!"

instagram:18086108894457086.caption:
Before Leamington RFC, there was Leamington Rovers.

Founded in 1876, 50 years before today’s club, they wore black shirts with a skull and crossbones on the front, played on Leam Terrace East, and had 100 members by 1879.

They reached the final of the inaugural Midland Counties Cup in 1882, losing to Moseley. They folded in 1886 when members stopped paying their subscriptions.

A century and a half on, the skull and crossbones returns. The Vets and the Lions have been wearing it on our centenary away strip, in tribute to the Rovers. 💙❤️💛

#LeamingtonRFC #LRFC100 #OneClubOneLeam

None of it would have been possible without the generosity of our donors. Swipe to see everyone who contributed, and if you spot a familiar name, give them some love.

instagram:18087204137222916.caption:
Today marks 56 years since Leamington RFC opened Moorefields.

The formal opening took place on 8th September 1970, conducted by Bill Ramsay, President of the RFU. The ground was named in honour of President Pip Moore, who had done so much to make the move possible. His term of office was extended to a third season so that he could preside over the opening of the ground that now bears his name.

Two representative sides played that day: a Leamington Invitation XV and a Warwickshire XV. Warwickshire won 22-6.

Who can spot an England international in a Leamington shirt? 👀

56 years later, it’s still home. 
💙❤️💛

instagram:18103222175059911.caption:
🧠🏉 CONCUSSION AWARENESS DAY | 18 SEPTEMBER

Rugby is a physical game. We love the competition, the tackles, the teamwork and everything that comes with being part of a rugby club.

But there is one thing that will always come before the game: our players' health.

WHAT IS CONCUSSION?
Concussion is a brain injury. It can happen after a direct blow to the head, but it can also happen following a hit to the body that causes the head and brain to move rapidly.

And importantly, you don't have to lose consciousness to have a concussion.

Headache, dizziness, confusion, memory problems, poor balance, nausea, feeling foggy or simply not seeming like themselves can all be signs that something isn't right.

That's why everyone at Leamington RFC needs to know the 4 Rs: players, parents, coaches, first aiders, therapists and supporters.

🧠 1. RECOGNISE
Know the signs and symptoms. If something doesn't look right, take it seriously.

🛑 2. REMOVE
If concussion is suspected, remove the player from play immediately. There is no "playing on" and no same-day return to rugby in community rugby.

❤️ 3. RECOVER
Concussion needs time and appropriate management. Recovery should never be rushed, and players should follow the appropriate graduated return-to-play process.

🏉 4. RETURN
Returning to rugby is the final step, when the player is ready and has completed the appropriate return-to-play process safely.

OUR COMMITMENT TO PLAYER WELFARE
At our club, concussion awareness isn't just something we talk about on one day of the year.

We are proud to have:
✔️ 4 qualified physios and sports therapists for senior and colts rugby
✔️ A qualified first aider for every age group
✔️ Coaches, first aiders and therapists completing RFU HEADCASE training every year
✔️ A commitment to following RFU and World Rugby guidance

Because concussion can affect players of every age, from our youngest age groups through to senior rugby, everyone has a part to play in recognising when something isn't right.

If in doubt, sit them out.

The match, the training session and the result can wait. The player's brain can't. 💙❤️💛

#OneClubOneLeam #ConcussionAwareness #Headcase #GrassrootsRugby

instagram:18116767087621694.caption:
Join us this weekend for our local derby against Old Leamingtonians and to remember the life of Peter. 

This weekend sees Leamington take on Old Leamingtonians at Moorefields. This time, though, there are more than league points and local bragging rights on offer as we contest the Peter Gray Memorial Cup for the first time.

As you will undoubtedly know, Peter was a legend of Leamington RFC, who enjoyed a storied playing career and was a passionate supporter and president of the club in his retirement.
Peter had a wealth of friends on both sides of the hedge, so it seemed the perfect fixture to remember Peter after he lost his long and brave battle with cancer last summer

Kick off on Saturday is 2:15, and we’d love to see the sidelines full of supporters from Leamington , Old Leamingtonians, and the game of rugby, which Peter was so passionate about.
Don’t forget to bring some cash with you, as there will be a collection for Myton Hospice, who supported the Gray family, who in turn have continued to raise money for the charity.

In 1978, Peter Preece joined Leamington RFC from Coventry. By then, his England career was already behind him: 12 caps, including wins on tour in South Africa and New Zealand.

At Coventry he’d made 185 appearances and scored over 100 tries. He also played for the Barbarians, crossing 5 times in 6 games, and narrowly missed out on the 1974 Lions tour through injury.

Here he is with club President Pip Moore and fellow England international Keith Savage, at a presentation at the club.

Peter kept playing for Leam into his 50s, before becoming club President in 2004. His son Adam followed him into a Leam shirt too, at full-back. 💙❤💛

instagram:18144619951605598.caption:
100 years ago today, Leamington RFC played its first game.

Saturday 25 September 1926. Coventry St Mark's were the visitors, and a good crowd turned out to watch.

It wasn't pretty. The local paper described a tight, scrappy contest fought out between the forwards, and St Mark's went in at half-time three points up.

After the break it was all Leamington. The pressure told on the right, and Russell went over almost exactly where the St Mark's try had come from. The conversion drifted just wide.

3-3. In the paper's words, "a well-fought game ended with honours even."

The first Leamington XV: Kench; Peers, Foss, Hughes, Price; Clow, Chapman; Lewis, Russell, Millen, Smith, Jacox, Walkley, Scovell, Barr.

Here's to the next 100. 💙❤️💛

122-0.

March 1980. The Spartans against Stratford. 24 tries. The referee stopped the game well before the 80-minute mark once he knew the club record had been beaten.

Pictured: the Spartans squad from that season. Not necessarily the exact side out on the day, but the team that made history.

instagram:18398353642082578.caption:
In winter 1949/50, Leamington RFC started using the gymnasium at Arnold Lodge School for training sessions.

Also using the gym was a young boxer from Leamington by the name of Randy Turpin.

The Leamington Licker.

A year or so later he would beat Sugar Ray Robinson at Earls Court to become world middleweight champion. Before that, he was practising his body shots on our players to toughen them up.

Photo: Turpin squaring up to scrum half Peter Jones, Arnold Lodge School gym. 💙❤️💛

instagram:18465033178102711.caption:
This Saturday at Moorefields.

From 12pm we’re hosting the Warwickshire Walking Rugby Festival on behalf of Warwickshire RFU. The festival has been going four years now, and we’ve won it twice. We’re back in it again this year, alongside clubs from across the county, and we’re proud to be hosting as part of our centenary celebrations.

Then at 3pm, we welcome San Isidro RFC, a touring side from Madrid, for a veterans’ fixture. Known back home as the Old Lizards, they’re here thanks to a club connection going back to 1994, when one of their players lined up alongside one of ours at Alcester. Thirty-odd years on, the friendship’s brought a Spanish touring team to Leamington.

All welcome for the rugby, all welcome for the social that follows. Come and be part of it.
💙❤️💛
